title: Listed HD 139139 dips fail a common-speed equal-area occultation test under Gaussian errors
abstract: We test a necessary depth-duration order for small opaque objects of equal area that cross one static star at one projected speed. The star must be no brighter towards its edge. The 28 listed HD 139139 dips give a conservative p-value bound of 1.44e-8 under unbiased Gaussian marginal errors of the listed size. A simultaneous input box covers the search over all event pairs and allows correlated errors. If equal area and one host are retained, the 95 percent lower bound on the projected-speed ratio is 2.113. Removal of the deepest dip gives p <= 0.447 and a speed lower bound of one. Thus the constraint is not robust to an arbitrary bad event. Doubled errors also remove rejection at 0.05. Fitted durations may differ from geometric crossing times. Instrument errors and selection remain open. No new dip, planet or independent confirmation is found. Original code, aggregate results, a static figure and external-source retrieval steps are included. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-899152a245de; topic astronomy; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: Conditional speed lower bounds change with the input error box. The ordering test fails to reject after removal of the deepest event. Equal area, one static host, small objects and Gaussian errors are necessary assumptions.
